title: Ernie Jr. rehearses an eighty-five-piece band for a young Black conductor
summary: Junior rounds up musicians in the union hall to proof a young conductor's music for the Hollywood Symphony.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: One thing that made me feel so happy in this thing, Ernie, this summer, I was talking about leaving and he said no, I want you to stay at least--he named the date, I think it was the second or third of July, he said I want you to hear this band, we're rehearsing about an eighty-five or ninety piece band. I said what is it, a concert? He said no, it was kind of like a dress rehearsal.

So anyway, we didn't go into detail, but that night I did go with him and so--I wish I knew him, I bet you'd know him--a young, black conductor, I think in his early thirties, is going to be guest conductor of the Hollywood Symphony and they were going to do some of his numbers, and some other special arrangements they had, and he wanted proof to be sure that everything was all right, he didn't want to carry it to this symphony, and they come

up and this is wrong. That night Ernie made me acquainted with him, he said I'm quite sure--naturally he laughed because your son would be proud of you but said, you should be extra proud of him and I said what do you mean? He said well, he called every one of these members and nobody that he called turned him down, unless they had a gig for that night. And so those friends that they have called him on gigs and he has called them and they were anxious, and of course he had all around, white and black, to do this proof, you know, read for him.
Yeah, that's what he was saying, that they did it gratis.

They got permission, it was in the union hall, where they were doing it, and so they got permission to be in there and do this and they did this gratis. He said to have that kind of friend, he said, really, I thought about who I

would have to do this and said I picked him out and I think I made a good pick, and he said in the next thing, he knows musicians. He said these people in here--not cause I'm talking to you--but whatever instrument they are here on, they play.
I remember when we were going that night, with all the horns they had, he picked up a bass clarinet and I says is that all you need? He said Yeah, I hope I can take care of it.
That's what everybody else said, it wasn't like you were just going to a dance, recording session or something, you better have your piccolo, your flute or all and everything.
He had them there on their specialty, the instrument they specialized in?
If you were a better flute player than you were a saxophone, you were there on flute?
And that's hard to do in California, because the musicians are very independent, so that was commendable.
I'm sure you might know him, but he's a young black in his early thirties and talking to Ernie after that, he was sensational.
